page.title: Behavioral Core
page.subtitle: Two passes, ~10 minutes. The first asks how others expect you to behave; the second asks who you really are. The gap between them tells the story.
page.intro: You'll see the same 86 adjectives twice. Pick the ones that fit — don't overthink. Click again to unselect.

selfConcept.title: Pass 1 of 2 — Self-Concept
selfConcept.instructions: Pick adjectives describing how others (managers, colleagues) expect you to behave at work.

self.title: Pass 2 of 2 — Self
self.instructions: Now pick the adjectives describing how you really are at work. Be honest, even if it diverges from the first list.

form.minimumHint: Pick at least {{min}} adjectives that describe you. Fewer than that and your profile will read as merely "balanced" — pick decisively.
form.minimumMet: Enough signal — you can continue or keep picking.

result.subtitle: Behavioral archetype
result.layer1Callout: Your 3-min read: {{triad}}. {{profile}} is the behavioral substrate underneath — the stable drives that make this leadership feel natural to you.
result.layer1Missing: Take the 3-minute Layer 1 first to see how your behavioral core shapes the leadership style you reach for.
result.drivesNote: Numbers blend who you are (60%) with how others expect you to be (40%).

factorInfo.dominance: Drive to control outcomes and people. High = takes charge and decides fast; low = collaborative and consensus-seeking.
factorInfo.extraversion: Drive for social interaction and influence. High = outgoing and persuasive; low = reserved and analytical.
factorInfo.patience: Drive for stability and steady pace. High = calm and methodical; low = fast-paced and urgent.
factorInfo.formality: Drive for structure and precision. High = process-oriented and detail-focused; low = flexible and improvising.

result.dominantNote: Great leaders don't pick a favorite club. The radar shows your full bag — but {{style}} is where you naturally reach.

diff.heading: How Layer 1 and Layer 2 align
diff.noLayer1: Take Layer 1 first to enable the side-by-side comparison.

verdict.aligned: ✓ Aligned — both layers point to {{style}} as your strongest pull. Your visible leadership matches your behavioral substrate.
verdict.softMismatch: ↗ Close — Layer 1 says you lead {{layer1}} but Layer 2's strongest is {{layer2}}. They're related — your behavioral drives support both styles.
verdict.stretching: ⚠ Divergent — Layer 1 says you lead {{layer1}} but Layer 2's strongest is {{layer2}}. You may be stretching beyond your natural drives — sustainable for short bursts, tiring over time.

ricercatore.name: The Researcher
ricercatore.description: Methodical and data-driven. Goes deep into every detail before deciding. Nothing is left to chance: gathers information, analyzes alternatives, then acts with surgical precision.
strengths: Ability to spot errors and inconsistencies
cautions: May seem detached or cold in relationships
Risk of analysis paralysis when decisions are urgent
Tendency to slow the team with requests for more data
ricercatore.idealEnvironment: Roles requiring research, data analysis, QA, or compliance. Structured environments with time to go deep.
ricercatore.communicationStyle: Prefers written, detailed communication. Appreciates facts and data, not generalizations. Respects those who come prepared.

direttore.name: The Director
direttore.description: Results above all else. Works with relentless precision and determination. Never settles, maintains total control over processes to ensure everything runs to their standards.
cautions: May be perceived as rigid or authoritarian
direttore.idealEnvironment: Technical leadership roles, project management, environments where precision is critical. Operational autonomy.
direttore.communicationStyle: Direct and concise. Doesn't enjoy small talk. Wants to know the 'what' and the 'when', not the 'how you feel'.

esperto.name: The Specialist
esperto.description: Deep expertise and meticulous work in specific areas. Would rather be the foremost expert in their field than a generalist. Work quality is their personal signature.
strengths: Ability to work in depth on complex topics
cautions: May struggle with roles requiring versatility
esperto.idealEnvironment: Highly specialized roles, research, environments that reward depth. Low role rotation.
esperto.communicationStyle: Precise and technical. Responds best to specific questions. Doesn't enjoy generic meetings or vague brainstorming.

visionario.name: The Strategist
visionario.description: Thinks big and plans long-term. Combines strategic vision with analytical rigor. Sees connections where others see chaos and turns complex ideas into structured action plans.
cautions: Sometimes perceived as detached from reality
visionario.idealEnvironment: Strategy roles, executive consulting, R&D. Environments that value long-term thinking.
visionario.communicationStyle: Selective communicator: speaks when they have something meaningful to say. Prefers intellectual debate to surface conversation.

pioniere.name: The Venturer
pioniere.description: Enterprising and oriented to immediate action. Challenges the status quo with courage and independence. Doesn't ask permission: acts, experiments, fails fast, restarts. Rules are suggestions.
cautions: May be too direct and brusque
pioniere.idealEnvironment: Startups, entrepreneurial roles, environments rewarding total autonomy. Low bureaucracy.
pioniere.communicationStyle: Ultra-direct. Few words, lots of facts. Doesn't tolerate long meetings or slow decision processes.

armonizzatore.name: The Harmonizer
armonizzatore.description: Builds team harmony naturally. Sociable, collaborative, and organized — the glue that holds the group together. Their mission: make everyone feel included, heard, and valued.
strengths: Ability to organize people and social processes
cautions: May sacrifice own needs for the team
armonizzatore.idealEnvironment: HR roles, community management, collaborative environments. Teams that need cohesion.
armonizzatore.communicationStyle: Warm and inclusive. Always asks how you are before talking work. Prefers face-to-face.

capitano.name: The Captain
capitano.description: Charismatic leader who guides with energy, vision, and powerful communication. Enters a room and dominates it naturally. Motivates teams through personal charisma and the ability to paint a compelling vision.
cautions: May dominate conversations and not listen
capitano.idealEnvironment: Executive leadership roles, dynamic and fast-changing environments. Crisis or transformation situations.
capitano.communicationStyle: Energetic and direct. Prefers communicating the vision over the details. Uses stories and metaphors.

mediatore.name: The Mediator
mediatore.description: Patient, empathetic, and consensus-oriented. The emotional glue of the team: listens to everyone, mediates between different positions, and creates a safe space where people can express themselves without fear.
strengths: Constant emotional support to the team
mediatore.idealEnvironment: Mediation roles, team support, environments requiring consensus. Flat organizations.
mediatore.communicationStyle: Gentle and patient. Asks open questions. Prefers dialogue over monologue. Never raises their voice.

ribelle.name: The Maverick
ribelle.description: Bold, charismatic, and intolerant of conventions. Combines the Captain's social energy with total aversion to rules. Challenges the status quo loudly and drags others into their revolutionary vision.
cautions: Impatient with any form of authority
ribelle.idealEnvironment: Early-stage startups, creative roles, environments rewarding disruption. Zero bureaucracy.
ribelle.communicationStyle: Overwhelming. Talks fast, thinks fast, acts fast. Doesn't filter much of what they say.

persuasore.name: The Persuader
persuasore.description: Born communicator with an innate ability to motivate and convince. Reads people like an open book and knows exactly which lever to pull to get the desired result. Tireless negotiator.
strengths: Ability to motivate individuals and teams
persuasore.idealEnvironment: Sales, business development, negotiation roles. Competitive, dynamic environments.
persuasore.communicationStyle: Adaptive: changes style depending on the interlocutor. Uses storytelling. Always 'on'.

ambasciatore.name: The Promoter
ambasciatore.description: Sociable, optimistic, and naturally connected to people. Builds wide relationships and promotes ideas with contagious enthusiasm. The ideal public face of any organization.
ambasciatore.idealEnvironment: Communication, PR, relational marketing roles. Social and creative environments.
ambasciatore.communicationStyle: Enthusiastic and informal. Prefers phone calls and in-person meetings. Emails short and positive.

camaleonte.name: The Adapter
camaleonte.description: Versatile and perfectly balanced across all factors. Adapts to any situation and team easily. Like a chameleon, takes on the color of the surrounding environment without losing their own identity.
strengths: Adaptability to diverse teams and cultures
Ability to mediate between opposite styles
cautions: May seem indecisive or lacking strong opinions
Risk of not standing out in any specific area
camaleonte.idealEnvironment: Roles requiring flexibility, changing environments, multidisciplinary teams.
camaleonte.communicationStyle: Adapts to the interlocutor's style. Can be formal or informal depending on context.

artigiano.name: The Artisan
artigiano.description: Precise, reflective, and meticulous in execution. Like a craftsman, turns every task into a finished work with maniacal attention to detail. Observes more than they speak, and notices things others miss.
cautions: May find it hard to communicate their ideas
artigiano.idealEnvironment: High-quality execution roles, stable environments with clear processes. Independent work.
artigiano.communicationStyle: Listens much, speaks little. When they speak, precise and pertinent. Prefers written instructions.

guardiano.name: The Guardian
guardiano.description: The pillar of the organization. Stable, structured, and completely reliable. Maintains procedures, protects standards, and ensures everything functions as it should. Without them, chaos would take over.
strengths: Absolute reliability — the rock of the team
Precision and strict respect for procedures
cautions: May seem excessively rigid or bureaucratic
guardiano.idealEnvironment: Compliance, operations, regulated environments. Roles where stability is fundamental.
guardiano.communicationStyle: Formal and structured. Prefers clear procedures. Appreciates advance notice and predictability.

operatore.name: The Operator
operatore.description: Cooperative, patient, and deeply concrete. Works with calm and consistency without ever losing their cool. The perfect team player: doesn't seek the spotlight but is indispensable to daily functioning.
strengths: Ability to maintain a productive routine
cautions: May avoid necessary conflicts for the team
Slow to act in urgent situations
Risk of not expressing their own opinions
operatore.idealEnvironment: Operational roles, support teams, environments requiring consistency. High-quality repetitive work.
operatore.communicationStyle: Informal and relaxed. Never forces a conversation. Available and patient.

individualista.name: The Individualist
individualista.description: Independent, methodical, and determined. Works best in complete autonomy where they can apply their deep competence without interference. Combines the Director's determination with the Specialist's patience.
individualista.idealEnvironment: Independent work, research, individual consulting. Minimal social interaction required.
individualista.communicationStyle: Minimal, functional communication. Prefers to work in silence. Responds to email, not chat.

studioso.name: The Scholar
studioso.description: Expert and rigorous, pursues knowledge with determination. Less patient than the Individualist, the Scholar has a faster rhythm but the same hunger for competence. Excels at turning knowledge into results.
cautions: Impatient with those who lack the same depth
studioso.idealEnvironment: Advanced research, strategic analysis, roles requiring intellectual depth.
studioso.communicationStyle: Precise and at times technical. Prefers substantial debates to casual conversation.
